tools.name: list_layers
tools.title: List layers
tools.description: List the layers of the open QGIS project that FilterMate knows, as {"layers": [...]}. Each layer has layer_id, name, provider_type, feature_count (-1 when unknown), geometry_type, crs_authid, layer_kind (vector, raster or point_cloud), has_active_filter and active_filter_expression (cut past 200 characters, with active_filter_expression_length: describe_layer gives it whole), visible (checked in the layer tree, with its groups) and group (the groups above it, joined by " / "). The layers come in the order of the layer tree, the one drawn on top first. "more" says how many matching layers were left out by limit. Call this first: the other tools take layer names or ids from it.

kind.description: Only the layers of this kind

name_contains.description: Only the layers whose name holds this text (case ignored)

tools.name: filter_status
tools.title: Filter status
tools.description: Snapshot of the filter session: status, active_filters ({layer name: subset string}), their count, last_applied_at / last_applied_layer / last_applied_source and last_error. Vector subset strings only. filter_state also covers raster and point cloud layers.

tools.name: filter_state
tools.title: Filter state
tools.description: Every layer FilterMate filters right now, of any kind, as {"layers": [...]}. Each row has layer_id, name, layer_kind, subset (the filter string, empty for a clipped raster; cut past 200 characters, with subset_length: describe_layer gives it whole) and derived (true when the layer reads a clipped copy of its source). Use it to check what a filter did, and to find out what a previous call did when a request timed out.

tools.name: list_favorites
tools.title: List favorites
tools.description: List the favorites (saved filters) of the FilterMate project, as {"favorites": [...]}. Each has favorite_id (what apply_favorite takes), name, description, layer_name and expression.

tools.name: describe_layer
tools.title: Describe a layer
tools.description: What a layer is and what a filter can test on it: its fields, bands or point attributes. Returns its kind, provider, CRS, geometry, feature_count, subset (current filter), place in the tree, extent (own CRS), style; for a vector, sql_dialect (the language of its filter), fields [{name, type, alias?, filterable?}] (filterable false: virtual or joined, a filter cannot test it), joins and relations; for a raster, bands [{band, name, classes}] and pixel_size; for a point cloud, attributes.

layer.description: Layer id or name, of any kind

tools.name: field_values
tools.title: Values of a field
tools.description: Distinct values a field takes in what the layer shows now, to write a filter with their exact spelling. Returns values, truncated, and minimum and maximum of a number or date; no NULL. Refused on web services.

tools.name: layer_statistics
tools.title: Statistics of a layer
tools.description: Count, sum, mean, minimum, maximum of a field or of the geometries of a layer, in all or by group, on what it shows or its selection: "how many", "what total", what a filter kept. Returns feature_count, statistics, unit, groups, groups_total, truncated, ranked_by. Refused on web services and above 500000 features: filter or select first.

field.description: Empty: count the features, or use measure

group_by.description: One row of statistics per value

measure.description: Of the geometries instead of a field: m (perimeter of polygons) or m2

tools.name: sample_features
tools.title: Sample of features
tools.description: A few features of a vector layer with their attributes, to see what its rows look like. Among the features the layer shows now (its filter applies). Returns crs_authid, features [{fid, attributes {field: value}, geometry {type, centroid, bbox}}], truncated (more features match), fields_truncated and scope. Long text is cut at 200 characters. A web service (WFS) is read only where the map shows it, without expression nor selection (scope: the features the map shows): zoom to the area first.

fields.description: Only these fields; the first 50 fields by default

expression.description: QGIS expression (NOT SQL) the features must match, as for select_features: "population" > 10000

geometry.description: Also the type, centroid and bounding box of each geometry, in the layer CRS

tools.name: identify_at
tools.title: Identify at a point
tools.description: What lies at a point of the map: the features of the vector layers and the values of the rasters there. As the Identify tool of QGIS. Returns layers, only those with something at the point: [{layer_name, layer_kind, features [{fid, attributes}], truncated}] for a vector layer, [{layer_name, layer_kind, values [{band, value}]}] for a raster; and skipped (web services, which are not read).

x.description: X or longitude of the point

y.description: Y or latitude of the point

crs.description: CRS of the point, such as EPSG:4326; the CRS of the map (canvas_crs of map_context) by default

layers.description: Only these layers (ids or names); the visible layers by default

tolerance.description: Search distance around the point, in the units of crs; five pixels of the map by default

limit.description: At most this many features per layer

tools.name: find_algorithms
tools.title: Find a Processing algorithm
tools.description: Find the Processing algorithms of QGIS the agent may run, by words of their id, name, group or tags. Only the algorithms of QGIS itself that make layers, or answer statistics, are listed: none that runs SQL or code, writes to a data source or a file, or reaches the network. Returns algorithms [{id, name, group, summary}] and total. Then describe_algorithm gives the parameters of one.

query.description: Words in English, as QGIS names its algorithms: buffer, centroids, dissolve, clip, join attributes, voronoi, heatmap, slope...

tools.name: describe_algorithm
tools.title: Describe a Processing algorithm
tools.description: What a Processing algorithm does, and how to give each of its parameters to run_algorithm. Returns help, parameters [{name, type, description, optional, default, options (an enum: give the index or the text), parent (the layer a field or a distance belongs to), minimum, maximum, value (how to give it), destination (an output: FilterMate writes it to a temporary layer)}] and outputs. left_out names parameters that cannot be given (files, folders, connections).

algorithm_id.description: Id from find_algorithms, such as native:buffer

tools.name: run_algorithm
tools.title: Run a Processing algorithm
tools.description: Run a Processing algorithm of QGIS on layers of the project; the layers it makes are added to the project. Each output layer is a temporary file: export_layers keeps one for good. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn removes them. Returns layers [{output, layer_id, name, layer_kind, feature_count}], values (what the algorithm answers besides layers: statistics...), not_made and messages (its warnings). Inputs are layers of the project only, never a path or a URL; expressions take the functions of select_features and math, text and geometry ones.

parameters.description: Values by parameter name, as describe_algorithm says: layers by name or id, {"layer": ..., "selected_only": true} for the selected features of a source, numbers, text, the index or the text of an option. Outputs are written by FilterMate: leave them out, or pass false to skip an optional one.

names.description: Name of the layer made by each output, by output name (OUTPUT...)

tools.name: preview_filter
tools.title: Try a filter
tools.description: Try an expression alone on a private copy of the layer, never combined with its filter: nothing changes. Returns valid, feature_count (-1: unknown) and error. Refused on web services and memory layers.

tools.name: map_context
tools.title: Map context
tools.description: What the user is looking at in QGIS. Returns project_crs, canvas_crs, extent_wkt (the visible extent, usable as is with geometry_filter and canvas_crs), extent (the same as [xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax]), scale, layouts (the print layouts of the project, by name), active_layer_id, active_layer_name, selections [{layer_id, name, selected_count}] (the layers with selected features, which cross_filter uses as its source) and drawn_objects [{layer_id, name, crs_authid, count, area_m2, extent_wkt}] (the rasters on which the user drew objects in the FilterMate dock: cross_filter uses them with that raster as source_layer and raster_selection {"dock_objects": true}). available is false when QGIS has no map canvas.

tools.name: apply_filter
tools.title: Apply a filter expression
tools.description: Set the filter (subset string) of one vector layer by its attributes; revert with clear_filters. Returns success, expression, replaced_filter (the filter it lost) and active_filters. GeoPackage and Shapefile may take an invalid expression silently and show nothing: a count of -1 or 0 says so, clear_filters recovers.

layer_name.description: A VECTOR layer id or name

expression.description: SQL WHERE clause without WHERE: "population" > 10000 AND "dep" = '31'. Comparisons, IN, LIKE, BETWEEN, IS NULL, simple functions; no subquery

operator.description: With the current filter: AND narrows, OR widens, AND NOT takes the condition out; omit to replace

tools.name: undo_filter
tools.title: Undo the last vector filter
tools.description: Undo the last step of the dock's vector filter history (the dock's Undo button). Returns the step rolled back to (layer_name, expression, is_clear) and active_filters. Only steps recorded by the dock itself are undone: nothing done through these tools (apply_filter, cross_filter, geometry_filter, point_cloud_filter, clear_filters, apply_favorite) is, so use clear_filters to revert those. Fails with 'Nothing to undo' when the history is empty. Not idempotent: each call undoes one more step, so after an error or a timeout read filter_state before calling again.

tools.name: redo_filter
tools.title: Redo the last undone vector filter
tools.description: Redo the step undone last in the dock's vector filter history (the dock's Redo button). Same answer and same caution as undo_filter (not idempotent: read filter_state after an error or a timeout). Fails with 'Nothing to redo' when there is nothing to redo.

tools.name: cross_filter
tools.title: Cross filter
tools.description: Filter layers of any kind (features, pixels, LiDAR points) by where they lie against the area of a source layer: a vector's selection, a raster's pixels, a point cloud's points. clear_filters reverts it. Returns filtered, failed, skipped and warnings ({layer: reason}; a warning: filtered, not exactly).

target_layers.description: Layers of any kind, not the source

predicates.description: Each tested as `target <predicate> source`, a target kept when any holds: Contain = the target contains the source, Are within = it lies inside, Disjoint = outside

buffer.description: Around the source, in metres (CRS units if projected); negative shrinks

coverage_min.description: Polygon targets: minimum % of the target inside the source

operator.description: With each target's filter: AND narrows, OR widens, AND NOT removes this selection (from the whole layer when unfiltered); omit to replace it

selected_only.description: Vector source: its selected features, else what its filter keeps (a WFS is never read whole); false: all it shows

anyOf.description: Pixels kept on a raster source (same rules as the EXPLORING raster panel of the dock).

mode.description: range: minimum to maximum, inclusive; classes: pixel values in classes

derivative.description: range: what the bounds apply to, the band read as a DTM

dock_objects.description: The objects drawn in the dock (drawn_objects); alone

raster_selection.description: REQUIRED for a raster source: the pixels that make the area

anyOf.description: Points kept on a point cloud (ASPRS classes, ranges, return number, expression).

classes.description: ASPRS codes: 2 ground, 3-5 vegetation, 6 building, 9 water

point_cloud_criteria.description: Point cloud source: the points that make the area (omit: those it shows)

filter_source.description: Raster source: mask it outside the selection too

tools.name: geometry_filter
tools.title: Filter by a WKT geometry
tools.description: cross_filter with a WKT geometry (an extent, a drawn area) instead of a source layer. Same effect and answer; not in the undo history (clear_filters reverts).

wkt.description: WKT; an extent as a rectangle POLYGON

predicates.description: Each tested as `target <predicate> source`, a target kept when any holds: Contain = the target contains the source, Are within = it lies inside, Disjoint = outside

buffer.description: In the CRS units of the first target

operator.description: With each target's filter: AND narrows, OR widens, AND NOT removes this selection (from the whole layer when unfiltered); omit to replace it

tools.name: point_cloud_filter
tools.title: Filter point clouds
tools.description: Keep only some points (class, elevation, intensity, return, expression) on point cloud layers, the same criteria on each (all the tiles of a LiDAR set). undo_filter does not undo it: clear_filters does. Returns done, failed and skipped.

classes.description: ASPRS codes: 2 ground, 3-5 vegetation, 6 building, 9 water

operator.description: With each target's filter: AND narrows, OR widens, AND NOT removes this selection (from the whole layer when unfiltered); omit to replace it

tools.name: clear_filters
tools.title: Clear filters
tools.description: Put layers back on their source with no filter (the dock's Unfilter): reverts cross_filter, geometry_filter, point_cloud_filter and apply_favorite. Returns done, failed and skipped.

tools.name: apply_favorite
tools.title: Apply a favorite
tools.description: Apply a saved favorite, as the dock's favorites menu does. Returns the step (layer_name, expression, is_clear) and active_filters. The favorite id must exist: use list_favorites first.

tools.name: zoom_to
tools.title: Zoom the map
tools.description: Zoom the map to a layer, its selection, a WKT extent, or everything (no argument); only the view changes. Returns extent_wkt and scale. Fails without a map window.

tools.name: select_features
tools.title: Select features
tools.description: Select the features of a vector layer matching a QGIS expression, as the user would in QGIS. A selection is not a filter: the features stay visible, they are highlighted. Use it to make the source of cross_filter (which uses the selected features), or when the user asks to select. Returns layer_name and selected_count. Comparisons, IN, LIKE and simple text, number, date and geometry functions are accepted; other functions are refused.

expression.description: QGIS expression (NOT SQL), plain conditions only: "population" > 10000, "nom" ILIKE 'saint%', area($geometry) > 1000. Field names in double quotes, text in single quotes.

clear.description: Empty the selection instead of selecting

add.description: Add to the current selection instead of replacing it

tools.name: set_layer_style
tools.title: Style a layer
tools.description: Change how a layer is drawn; replaces its style. Undoing the turn of the chat brings the previous style back.

mode.description: Points only: heatmap, point_cluster, point_displacement. Polygons only: dot_density, 2.5d. Raster: pseudocolor, gray, hillshade. keep: opacity and blend alone

items.description: A condition and the color of what it keeps.

expression.description: QGIS condition (NOT SQL): "population" > 10000; empty: every other feature

rules.description: A feature takes the first rule it matches; end with an empty expression, or the rest is not drawn

field.description: Classes, sizes, dots; heatmap: weight; 2.5d: height

ramp.description: Viridis, Spectral, Blues, RdBu, YlOrRd, Magma... Terrain for relief

cut.description: Raster: % left out at each end of the ramp

width.description: mm: line, point, heatmap radius, cluster distance, largest size

blend.description: multiply darkens (a hillshade over colors); empty: unchanged

z_factor.description: hillshade (2 or 3 for a flat relief), 2.5d: stretch

tools.name: set_labels
tools.title: Label a layer
tools.description: Write a field or an expression next to the features of a vector layer, or turn the labels off. Undoing the turn of the chat brings the previous labels back.

placement.description: Lines: curved (rivers), parallel, horizontal. Polygons: centroid, horizontal, free, around, perimeter. Points: around

tools.name: update_features
tools.title: Edit attributes of features
tools.description: Change attribute values of features, in the edit buffer of the layer: nothing is saved. The layer goes into editing mode; the user reviews the changes and saves them (Save Layer Edits) or discards them. Choose the features with expression and/or selected_only. Keys, joined and virtual fields are not changed; a value that does not fit its field is refused. Returns changed (features), editing and unsaved. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn takes the changes back while they are not saved.

values.description: Field: value, each converted to the type of its field (a number, a text, true or false, null)

formulas.description: Field: QGIS expression computed on each feature, such as "pop" * 2 or round($area / 10000, 2)

expression.description: QGIS expression choosing the features ("nom" = 'Muret'); the expression true for every feature

tools.name: delete_features
tools.title: Delete features
tools.description: Delete features of a vector layer, in its edit buffer: they are gone from the data once the user saves. Only when the user asks to delete features; to hide them, filter the layer instead. The chat of FilterMate asks the user first. Returns deleted, editing and unsaved.

tools.name: add_features
tools.title: Add features
tools.description: Add features to a vector layer from WKT geometries and attributes, in its edit buffer: nothing is saved. Returns added, editing and unsaved. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn takes them back while they are not saved.

features.description: [{"wkt": "POINT(1.44 43.6)", "attributes": {"nom": "Puits"}}]: geometries of the type of the layer, coordinates in crs (the CRS of the layer by default; degrees only with EPSG:4326)

crs.description: CRS of the WKT, such as EPSG:4326; the layer's by default

tools.name: create_layout
tools.title: Make a print layout
tools.description: Make a print layout of the map (title, legend, scale bar, north arrow), added to the project for the user to finish; export_layout writes it to a file. Undoing the turn of the chat removes it. Returns name, items, extent_from and the scale of its map.

layers.description: Default: those checked in the tree

extent.description: xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, project CRS; default: extent_layer, then the view

extent_layer.description: Show the whole of this layer

template.description: A template of the profile (describe_layout lists them): its page and items instead

tools.name: export_layout
tools.title: Export a print layout
tools.description: Write a print layout of the project as PDF, PNG, JPG, SVG or TIFF in a sub-folder of the export root. A file of the same name there is kept: the new one is named <name>_2, <name>_3...; an image or SVG has one file per page. With atlas, a new folder <name>_atlas holds its pages (200 at most). The chat of FilterMate asks the user first. Returns path (relative to the sub-folder), bytes, and files and pages when several.

name.description: A layout of the project (map_context lists them)

subfolder.description: Sub-folder of the export root (a/b allowed, no ..)

georeference.description: PDF: georeferenced; image: a world file beside it

atlas.description: One page per feature of its atlas (set_atlas)

single_file.description: Atlas in PDF: one file; false: one per feature

tools.name: describe_layout
tools.title: Read a print layout
tools.description: What a print layout holds: pages [{page, width_mm, height_mm}], items [{ref, type, page, x_mm, y_mm, width_mm, height_mm, and scale and layers of a map, text of a text}] and its atlas. Without a name, layouts and templates (the .qpt of the profile).

name.description: A layout; empty: list the layouts and templates

tools.name: edit_layout
tools.title: Change a print layout
tools.description: Change a print layout item by item, all or none: add a text ([% "nom" %] follows an atlas), a map (extent_layer, or overview_of a map: a map of situation), a legend, scale bar or north arrow (of map), an attribute table (layer, columns, max_rows), a frame or a page; move, remove; set_text, set_map (layers, extent_layer, scale). Items by ref (describe_layout); x, y, width, height in mm from the top left of page. Returns done and items. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn puts the layout back.

tools.name: set_atlas
tools.title: Set the atlas of a layout
tools.description: Turn the atlas of a print layout on: one page per feature of a vector layer as filtered now, its map following each feature; export_layout with atlas writes them. Returns pages, maps and map_mode. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn puts the layout back as it was.

coverage_layer.description: Vector layer: one page per feature, as filtered now

hide_coverage.description: Hide the coverage layer on the maps

map_mode.description: auto: each feature plus margin; fixed: the scale of the map; predefined: the scales of the project

file_name.description: Expression naming the file of each page

maps.description: refs of the maps that follow; default: the largest

tools.name: set_project_crs
tools.title: Set the CRS of the project
tools.description: Set the CRS of the project, which the map follows: what the user calls changing the CRS of the view. Layers in other CRS are reprojected on the fly, their data does not change. Returns crs, description, units, geographic and previous. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn brings the previous CRS back.

crs.description: EPSG:2154 (Lambert-93), EPSG:4326 (WGS 84), EPSG:3857 (Web Mercator), an EPSG code alone, a PROJ: string from suggest_crs, or a layer of the project whose CRS is taken

tools.name: suggest_crs
tools.title: Suggest projections
tools.description: Projections suited to where the data lie and what the map is for, best first: the official system of the country, the local zone (UTM, Lambert CC), continental or world ones, and projections made for the data (PROJ: strings). Each says what it keeps. Returns bounds_wgs84, scale, current and suggestions [{crs, name, keeps, why, units}], each crs usable by set_project_crs. It changes nothing.

layers.description: Default: the layers shown, then the view

purpose.description: areas: equal-area; distances; shapes: conformal; world; web

tools.name: make_cartogram
tools.title: Make a cartogram
tools.description: Make a new layer whose areas show a quantity of a layer as filtered now (a population, votes...), not the land. Returns layer, kind, features, crs, and error_before / error_after (1 is exact). In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn removes the layer.

kind.description: contiguous: polygons deformed, borders kept; noncontiguous: each scaled; dorling: circles; demers: squares

tools.name: design_style
tools.title: Design a style
tools.description: Compose a finished style for a vector layer from a validated palette: one symbol, categories or classes, a look per geometry, SVG icons in the colour of their category, a variant for the map. Returns colors and problems (what readers with a colour deficiency cannot tell apart). Undone with the turn in the chat.

look.description: polygon: flat, outlined, hatched; line: flat, casing, halo, dashed; point: flat, icon, badge

icon.description: icon, badge: a word of an SVG of QGIS

tools.name: list_palettes
tools.title: List palettes
tools.description: The palettes design_style takes, by the job of their colours, with source, licence and problems.

tools.name: add_field
tools.title: Add a field
tools.description: Add a field to a vector layer, in its edit buffer: nothing is saved until the user saves the layer edits. With a formula the field is filled on every feature at once. Returns layer_name, field, type, computed (the features filled), and formula_error when the formula was refused (the field is then added, empty). In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn removes the field.

length.description: Length of a text field; 0 lets the source choose

formula.description: QGIS expression computing the value of each feature ("pop" / $area * 1000000, upper("nom")); empty leaves the field empty

tools.name: join_layers
tools.title: Join a layer
tools.description: Join two layers by a field: the fields of join_layer show beside each feature of layer whose target_field equals its join_field, as the Joins tab of the layer properties does. Nothing is written to either source. Returns layer_name, join_layer and fields_added (as they are named in layer). In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn removes the join.

layer.description: Layer that gets the fields (id or name)

join_layer.description: Layer whose fields are shown beside it, a table without geometry too (id or name)

fields.description: Fields of join_layer to show; all of them by default

prefix.description: Put before the names of the fields shown; the name of join_layer and _ by default

tools.name: set_form
tools.title: Set the form of a layer
tools.description: Set how fields show in the attribute form of a layer, all or none; only what an entry gives changes, "" removes. Nothing is written to the data. Returns layer_name and fields. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn puts the form back.

enforce.description: Constraints refuse to save; default: they warn

tools.name: relations
tools.title: Relations of the project
tools.description: The relations of the project: list, add or remove. The form of a parent lists its children. Nothing is written to the data. Returns relations [{id, name, parent, child, fields, strength}], or the relation added or removed. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn takes it back.

action.description: add: each child feature points to a parent feature by a field

name.description: add: its name; remove: its id or name

parent_field.description: add: its key, such as insee

strength.description: composition: children deleted with their parent

tools.name: group_layers
tools.title: Put layers in a group
tools.description: Organize the layer tree: put layers in a group, made where it is missing, first or last of it; or just above another layer, to draw them over it. Layers keep their data, style and visibility. Returns group, groups_made, moved and not_found. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn puts each layer back and removes the groups it made.

layers.description: Layer ids or names, in the order they take in the group

group.description: Group path from the top of the layer tree, such as Base or Base/Roads (made where missing); empty: the top of the tree itself

at_top.description: Put them first in the group (true) or last (false)

above.description: A layer: put them just above it, in its group, so they are drawn over it; group and at_top are then not used

tools.name: rename_layer
tools.title: Rename a layer
tools.description: Give a layer of the project another name, as shown in the layer tree and the legend; its data and source do not change. With group, rename a group of the layer tree instead. Returns layer_id, name and previous.

group.description: true: layer is the path of a group of the layer tree (Base/Roads), and that group is renamed

tools.name: bookmark
tools.title: Spatial bookmarks
tools.description: Spatial bookmarks of the project: named places the user goes back to (Bookmarks panel of QGIS). Returns action, name, bookmarks (all names), replaced, and extent_wkt after a zoom. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn brings the bookmarks back as they were.

action.description: list the bookmarks; add one (the visible map, or extent_wkt; replaces a bookmark of that name); zoom the map to one; remove one

name.description: Name of the bookmark, for every action but list

extent_wkt.description: For add: the area as WKT (its bounding box is kept); the visible map by default

crs.description: CRS of extent_wkt; the CRS of the map by default

tools.name: map_theme
tools.title: Map themes
tools.description: Map themes of the project: saved views of which layers are shown, with their styles, used by layouts and by the user to switch views. Returns action, name, themes (all of them), replaced and layers_shown. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn brings the themes, the visibility and the styles back.

action.description: list the themes; save the layers shown now and their styles under a name (replaces a theme of that name); apply a theme to the map; remove a theme

name.description: Name of the theme, for every action but list

tools.name: set_layers_visibility
tools.title: Show or hide layers
tools.description: Check or uncheck layers in the layer tree (shown or hidden on the map). Returns done and failed.

visible.description: true shows the layers, false hides them

tools.name: layer_options
tools.title: Options of a layer in the panels
tools.description: What a layer shows in FilterMate's EXPLORING panel and its FILTERING options, with the values each takes; panel: whether EXPLORING shows it now, and then the buttons of its rail (set_exploring). Needs FilterMate's panel open.

tools.name: set_layer_options
tools.title: Set the options of layers in the panels
tools.description: Set, all or none, what layers show in FilterMate's EXPLORING panel and their FILTERING options, as the user would in the panel. exploring: single_selection_expression and multiple_selection_expression (a field of the layer), custom_selection_expression (a QGIS expression), current_exploring_groupbox (single_selection, multiple_selection, custom_selection), is_tracking, is_linking. filtering: layers_to_filter, geometric_predicates, source_layer_combine_operator and other_layers_combine_operator (AND, AND NOT, OR), buffer_value (metres), buffer_type (Round, Flat, Square), buffer_segments, and the has_... box of each. Returns changed and shown_in_panel.

layers.description: [{layer, exploring, filtering}], each a vector layer id or name with the options to set

reason.description: Why, in the language of the user

tools.name: set_exploring
tools.title: Drive the EXPLORING panel
tools.description: Drive FilterMate's EXPLORING panel live, as the user does: show a layer in it, set what its panel keeps (the range of a raster on its histogram, the classes or ranges of a point cloud), turn the buttons of its rail on or off, press zoom or identify. The names of the buttons of each kind of layer: skill panels. One tool on the map at a time: it waits for the user's click, so say what to click. A button the user hid, or greyed, is refused: say so. In FilterMate's chat, undone with the turn. Returns layer_name, kind, in_view, tools (on, off, press, hidden, unavailable), changed, pressed, values.

layer.description: Layer to show in EXPLORING, id or name; default: the one it shows

tools.description: Buttons of the rail on (true) or off (false)

show.description: Open EXPLORING in front: only when the user asks to see it

raster.description: band, quantity (value, slope_degrees, slope_percent, aspect, hillshade, roughness), minimum, maximum (null: no bound)

tools.name: export_options
tools.title: Export options of the panel
tools.description: How the project exports from FilterMate's EXPORTING panel, with the formats it takes. Needs the panel.

tools.name: set_export_options
tools.title: Set the export options of the panel
tools.description: Prepare FilterMate's EXPORTING panel, all or none, for the user to export from it; this exports nothing (export_layers does). Returns changed and saved.

changes.description: layers_to_export, datatype_to_export (format), projection_to_export (EPSG:...), styles_to_export (QML, SLD), output_folder_to_export, zip_to_export (.zip path), batch_output_folder, batch_zip, and the has_... box of each

reason.description: Why, in the language of the user

tools.name: segment_objects
tools.title: Draw objects with SAM
tools.description: Draw with SAM, on a raster, the object each feature of a guide layer points at, as a new polygon layer with the guide's attributes, sam_score and, for footprints, sam_iou (low: a footprint to look at, no proof of a change). Good on buildings, not on parcels or trees. Returns layer, guide_features, drawn, without_object, sam_score, sam_iou, seconds and stopped_early (the 20 s ran out: call again with fewer). QGIS is held about 2 s per 1024-pixel window. SAM is installed from the dock.

raster.description: An orthophoto, as on the map

guide_layer.description: Points (a click on each object) or polygons (footprints)

selected_only.description: Its selection; with none, what it shows (a web service needs one)

limit.description: A guide that gives more is refused

tools.name: similar_objects
tools.title: Find objects like an example with SAM
tools.description: Find with SAM, on a raster, the objects that look like an example (0.5 to 2 times its area), as a new layer with appearance (0 to 1) and area_m2. About half is right and most are missed: no census, the user checks. Give only the place meant: past 20 s it stops, above 64 windows of 1024 pixels it is refused. Returns layer (null: nothing found), objects, windows, stopped_early, seconds, examples and appearance. SAM is installed from the dock.

raster.description: An orthophoto, as on the map

example_layer.description: Its ONE selected feature (point or footprint) is the example

use_dock_object.description: The examples: the objects drawn in the dock (drawn_objects of map_context)

extent_wkt.description: Area searched (map_context's extent_wkt, its canvas_crs as extent_crs); empty: the map

tools.name: add_layer
tools.title: Add a layer
tools.description: Add a layer to the open project from a local file or a public https URL. Typical use after search_open_data: pick a geojson or gpkg resource url and add it, then filter it like any other layer. A remote file is read where it is when its server gives parts of it (GeoPackage, GeoTIFF, zip); any other is first copied to the QGIS profile (512 MB and 3 minutes at most). When it cannot be added the error says why: try another resource of the dataset, or a service layer. Returns the layer summary (layer_id, name, layer_kind, provider_type, crs_authid, feature_count). The chat of FilterMate asks the user first.

source.description: A local data file on the QGIS machine (gpkg, shp, geojson, json, kml, gml, gpx, fgb, csv, xlsx, parquet, tif, or a point cloud: las, laz, copc.laz; a GeoPackage table with |layername=name), or a public https URL of a vector or raster file (a resource url from search_open_data). Nothing else: no http, no provider URI, no database connection.

name.description: Name of the layer in the project (default: the file name)

kind.description: vector (default), raster, or point_cloud (a local las or laz file is one whatever is given here)

tools.name: add_service_layer
tools.title: Add a layer of a web service
tools.description: Add a layer of a WFS, WMS or WMTS service, read from the service as the map moves. A WFS layer is data, filtered on the server. A WMS or WMTS layer is an image drawn by the service (old maps, orthophotos of a year, cadastre, land cover): put under the other layers, it has no values to filter, read nor export. Only a layer the service lists can be added. Returns the layer summary. The chat of FilterMate asks the user first.

platform.description: A WFS, WMS or WMTS platform the user allowed, e.g. ign_wfs (IGN Géoplateforme, data), ign_wmts or ign_wms (IGN Géoplateforme, images)

typename.description: Layer id given by search_open_data on that platform, e.g. ADMINEXPRESS-COG-CARTO.LATEST:commune

name.description: Name of the layer in the project (default: its title)

tools.name: add_basemap
tools.title: Add a web basemap
tools.description: Add a web basemap (XYZ tiles) to the project, under every other layer. A basemap is an image drawn by its server as the map moves: a background, with no values to filter, read nor export. Only a basemap of the list can be added, and in the chat of FilterMate only one the user ticked; an address is never written here. Returns the layer summary. The chat of FilterMate asks the user first.

platform.description: A basemap the user allowed: osm_tiles (OpenStreetMap), carto_light (neutral light grey), carto_light_nolabels (the same with no place names, under layers that have labels), carto_dark, carto_voyager, ign_plan and ign_ortho (France: map and aerial photographs), google_satellite (worldwide satellite and aerial photographs), opentopomap (relief), or one the user added, by the name the chat lists it under

name.description: Name of the layer in the project (default: its title)

tools.name: add_elevation
tools.title: Add the elevation of an area
tools.description: Add the elevation of an area to the project as a raster layer (a digital elevation model), read from an elevation source the user allowed. Written on a grid in metres, added under the data and above the basemaps. Then set_layer_style (pseudocolor or hillshade) and contour_lines. Returns layer_id, name, crs_authid, resolution, minimum, maximum and mean (the heights, in metres) and note. The chat of FilterMate asks the user first.

extent_wkt.description: The area as WKT: the extent_wkt of find_place or of map_context. Empty: the visible map

crs.description: CRS of extent_wkt: EPSG:4326 for find_place; the CRS of the map when empty

platform.description: An elevation source the user allowed: copernicus_dem (worldwide, 30 m)

resolution.description: Pixel size in metres (default 30, coarser for a large area)

target_crs.description: A CRS in metres to write in (default: the project's when its projection keeps angles, as UTM, Lambert conformal or a stereographic does, else the UTM zone)

name.description: Name of the layer in the project

tools.name: add_population
tools.title: Add the population of an area
tools.description: Add the people of an area to the project as a raster of people per pixel, read from a population source the user allowed: how many live there, where they are dense. Pixels are summed, never averaged. Returns layer_id, total (the people of the rectangle around the area), maximum (in one pixel), resolution and note. The chat of FilterMate asks the user first.

extent_wkt.description: The area as WKT: the extent_wkt of find_place or of map_context. Empty: the visible map

crs.description: CRS of extent_wkt: EPSG:4326 for find_place; the CRS of the map when empty

platform.description: A population source the user allowed: meta_population (most countries, 30 m)

resolution.description: Pixel size in metres: 100 by default (a street), 1000 for a region

name.description: Name of the layer in the project

tools.name: add_osm_features
tools.title: Add OpenStreetMap features
tools.description: Add the OpenStreetMap features that carry given tags in an area (buildings, roads, hospitals, shops, parks...), anywhere, in EPSG:4326 with osm_id, name and a column per key (addr:street: addr_street). A town or a district, not a region. Returns layers [{layer_id, name, geometry, feature_count, fields}] and feature_count.

tags.description: Features with ONE of these tags: [{"key": "amenity", "value": "hospital"}], [{"key": "building"}]

items.description: One OpenStreetMap tag asked: a key, and a value or nothing for any value.

key.description: As OpenStreetMap writes it: amenity, building, highway, shop, landuse, addr:street

value.description: hospital, primary...; empty: any value of the key

extent_wkt.description: extent_wkt of find_place or map_context; empty: the map

crs.description: CRS of extent_wkt: EPSG:4326 for find_place; the CRS of the map when empty

geometry.description: as_mapped: a layer per geometry; points: one point each, to count or for a heatmap

tools.name: contour_lines
tools.title: Draw contour lines
tools.description: Draw the contour lines of an elevation raster of the project as a new line layer, added on top. Each line has elevation (its height) and is_index (1 for an index contour); the layer comes in thin lines with the index contours thicker. A temporary file: export_layers keeps it. Returns layer_id, name, feature_count, index_count, left_out, minimum and maximum (the levels drawn).

layer.description: Raster layer id or name: an elevation model (the layer of add_elevation)

interval.description: Height between two contours, in the units of the raster: 25 for a line every 25 m

index_interval.description: Height between two index contours, a multiple of interval (100)

min_length.description: Closed contours shorter than this are left out (default: ten pixels; 0 keeps all)

tools.name: duplicate_layer
tools.title: Duplicate a layer
tools.description: Add a second layer on the same data as a layer, with its style and filter, just above it: for what one layer cannot show at once (an elevation as colors and as a hillshade). Returns its summary.

layer.description: Vector or raster layer id or name

tools.name: local_copy
tools.title: Copy a web service layer locally
tools.description: Copy a web service layer over an area to a file next to the project (GeoPackage for features, GeoTIFF for a web map), and the layer reads it with its style and filter: faster, and without the network. A web map is copied as a still image at the finest level the budget affords. Returns reads, file, feature_count or resolution, complete and notes. OpenStreetMap and Google tiles are refused. The chat of FilterMate asks the user first.

layer.description: Layer id or name of a web service: WFS, OGC API Features, WMS, WMTS or XYZ tiles

action.description: copy: read the service over the area into a file the layer then reads; back: the layer reads its service again (the file stays); again: copy the area of its copy anew, the old file replaced

extent_wkt.description: The area as WKT (the extent_wkt of find_place or map_context). Empty: the visible map

crs.description: CRS of extent_wkt: EPSG:4326 for find_place; the CRS of the map when empty

tools.name: search_imagery
tools.title: Search satellite imagery
tools.description: Find satellite scenes over an area, newest first, with the GeoTIFF of each one. Returns datasets [{id, publisher (collection), description (date and cloud cover), resources: [{format, url}]}]; format visual is the natural colour image. Then add_layer with its url and kind raster.

bbox.description: [west, south, east, north] in degrees; omit for the current map extent

platform.description: STAC catalog the user allowed, e.g. earth_search

tools.name: remove_layers
tools.title: Remove layers
tools.description: Remove layers from the project, only when the user asks to remove them: never to hide or to filter a layer (set_layers_visibility, apply_filter). Their files are not deleted. The chat of FilterMate asks the user first, and undoing the turn there brings the layers back with their styles and filters, except a layer held in memory, whose features are lost. From another client it cannot be undone. Returns done and failed.

layers.description: Layer ids or names to remove from the project

tools.name: search_open_data
tools.title: Search open data
tools.description: Search datasets on an open data platform the user allowed, and get the URLs a layer can be made of. Returns datasets [{id, title, publisher, description, page, resources: [{title, format, url}]}], the resources kept to files add_layer can open (geojson, gpkg, zip, csv, tif...). Then add_layer with a resource url (geojson or gpkg first), or add_service_layer with the id on a WFS, WMS or WMTS platform. The query is sent to the platform.

query.description: Words to search, in the language of the platform

platform.description: datagouv (data.gouv.fr, France), opendatasoft (the public Opendatasoft hub), ign_wfs (IGN Géoplateforme layers), or a portal the user allowed

tools.name: find_place
tools.title: Find a place
tools.description: Find where a place is, by its name or its address, on a geocoder the user allowed. Returns places [{name, label, kind, longitude, latitude, extent_wkt}], the best match first. To show one, call zoom_to with its extent_wkt and crs EPSG:4326. When several places could be the one meant, ask the user which. The query is sent to the geocoder; nothing of the project is.

query.description: The name of a place or an address, as the user wrote it: Toulouse, 12 rue de la Paix Paris

platform.description: A geocoder the user allowed: ign_geocoder (IGN Géoplateforme: France, addresses and communes), photon (worldwide, from OpenStreetMap)

tools.name: export_layers
tools.title: Export filtered layers
tools.description: Write layers, as filtered now, to files on the QGIS machine below its export root; a file of the same name is overwritten, a zip never. Returns done, outputs ({layer name: file}), package, tables, styles, failed and skipped.

layers.description: Of any kind, one file each

subfolder.description: Below the export root: a or a/b, letters, digits, _ . - only

single_file.description: GPKG: all vector layers in one

package_name.description: Of the zip or single GPKG
